transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~61 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Mark Holloway (Silvergate Head of ML), Sara Gomez (Silvergate Platform Eng), Tara Singh (Silvergate CTO)
Shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/silvergate-poc, benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/silvergate-template.xlsx

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling: QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, baseline benchmarks, and timeline for a 4-6 week pilot. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for payments NLP workloads.

Topics: workload breakdown, latency/cost tradeoffs, sample size for benchmarks, security/VPC considerations, timeline and success criteria

[00:00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, quick intros, and then dig into the workload signals you can share and how we'll scope the benchmark
[00:00:18] Mark Holloway: thanks alex, hi team, im Mark, Head of ML -- our goal is to validate latency and cost for our fraud-detection assistant and payment reconciliation summarizer, and understand whether we need dedicated capacity or can use hosted
[00:00:35] Sara Gomez: hi all, sara here, platform eng, i'll own the integration bits for our staging environment and networking for the VPC if we go that route
[00:00:45] Priya Patel: great, so high level can you walk through your expected traffic shape, like average QPS, peak, concurrency and typical request sizes, that helps us recommend model variants and infra
[00:00:58] Mark Holloway: sure, rough numbers: average QPS around 18-25, peak QPS up to 120 for a 10-15 minute burst during business hours, concurrency around 30-45 at peak, steady off-peak under 5, daily pattern skewed to 08:30-11:30 and 14:00-16:00 UTC, weekends low
[00:01:22] Alex Chen: ok that peak to 120 is useful, do you have token histograms? like median input tokens, 95th, response sizes
[00:01:30] Mark Holloway: we have some rough histograms: median input tokens ~28, mean ~45, 95th at about 420 tokens (long receipts and attached notes), output tokens avg 70, 95th 600 for long summaries. Most requests are short Q&A style, about 75-80% under 80 input tokens
[00:01:54] Liam O'Neill: cool, that distribution suggests batching will help cost for embeddings and light generation, but for interactive latencies we'll need small batch sizes and low-concurrency instance types
[00:02:12] Sara Gomez: can you clarify the difference we'd see between hosted and dedicated for this workload? we're sensitive to p99 latency under 600ms for short responses
[00:02:22] Priya Patel: hosted can usually hit those latencies for typical short requests using optimized models, but if you want predictable p95/p99 under sustained peaks at 120qps, Dedicated or Reserved capacity gives stronger SLO guarantees. Private VPC adds networking overhead — usually +20-50ms depending on routing and whether H100 is colocated with your VPC egress
[00:02:48] Mark Holloway: what about quantization and model variants — we want to compare cost/perf tradeoffs, e.g., 8-bit quantized Llama-variant vs a 16-bit dense smaller model
[00:02:58] Alex Chen: yes, we'll include a matrix: model size (7B/13B/70B), quantization (int8/4-bit where supported), and kernel optimizations. We'll run baseline throughput and latency tests on A100 and H100 if you want to include both. Also we'll show estimated tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens for each config
[00:03:18] Mark Holloway: perfect. For POC success criteria, internally we care about: 1) p95 latency < 450ms for <100 token outputs in 90% of requests; 2) cost per 1M tokens below our current vendor by at least 20%; 3) integration into our VPC and KMS for secrets
[00:03:38] Alex Chen: good, we'll capture that as suggested success criteria and align on pass/fail thresholds before the run

[00:05:10] (discussion on benchmark methodology)
[00:05:10] Priya Patel: proposed benchmark steps: a) collect 7 days of production traffic samples (anonymized) b) generate synthetic load preserving token distribution and timestamp patterns c) run microbenchmarks for cold-start and steady-state d) run 10k-50k request end-to-end runs to measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput e) validate security/integration
[00:05:35] Mark Holloway: we can export logs; i'll ask infra to strip PII and provide a zipped histogram + sample payloads, aim to have that by friday
[00:05:47] Sara Gomez: for the VPC test we need a staging subnet and a short-lived test account, what's the typical setup time?
[00:05:55] Liam O'Neill: usually 2-3 business days after creds and network CIDR, we set up a secure peering and test connectivity. If you have strict egress policies we'll need an allowlist for Redwood test IPs

[00:07:00] (traffic modeling details)
[00:07:00] Alex Chen: on modeling traffic, we typically ask for: QPS time series (1-min granularity), histogram of input tokens, histogram of output tokens, percent of requests that require tool-calling or longer context (KV cache usefulness), and identify any long-tail flows that dominate cost
[00:07:22] Mark Holloway: most calls are stateless, but about 12% use convo context up to 2048 tokens for multi-turn investigations, could matter for KV cache and memory footprint
[00:07:34] Priya Patel: noted — we'll include tests with and without KV cache. For multi-turn profiles, the effective memory and latency can increase if you need to rehydrate caches across requests

[00:08:15] (benchmark sizing and sample sizes)
[00:08:15] Priya Patel: recommended sample sizes: for latency percentiles aim for at least 10k requests per model/config to get stable p99 numbers; for throughput we do sustained 15-minute runs at target QPS and a spike test that replicates your 10-15 minute bursts to observe autoscaling and tail-latency behavior
[00:08:36] Alex Chen: we'll include costs and estimated GPU hours per config so you can compare e.g., 13B int8 on A100 vs 70B 4-bit on H100 for the same workload

[00:09:30] (security and compliance)
[00:09:30] Tara Singh: security question, we need SOC 2 attestations, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs retention — do you ship logs we can ingest?
[00:09:40] Liam O'Neill: yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC support and audit logs with configurable retention. For Private deployments we can integrate your KMS/HSM and keep keys in your control
[00:09:55] Sara Gomez: network latency for VPC — you said +20-50ms typical, can you provide measurement plan?
[00:10:03] Priya Patel: we'll run synthetic pings and small token back-and-forth tests from your staging subnet to quantify RTT and add that to the report

[00:12:00] (cost optimization conversation)
[00:12:00] Alex Chen: optimization levers: prefix caching for repeated merchant queries, batch sizing for embedding/light inference, quantization, and routing to lower-cost model variants on non-critical paths. We'll model cost/latency tradeoffs and show marginal cost curves
[00:12:25] Mark Holloway: how set up for autoscaling and can we reserve burst capacity for payroll days?
[00:12:33] Priya Patel: dedicated pools support reserved burst capacity and policy-based routing. For payroll days we can create scheduled capacity reservations and test burst policies during the POC

[00:15:00] (bench specifics and timeline)
[00:15:00] Alex Chen: proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) - kickoff and data sharing; Week 1 - baseline runs and small microbenchmarks; Week 2 - sustained throughput and spike tests; Week 3-4 - integration and VPC proof; Week 4-6 - pilot and handoff to SRE if successful. So 4-6 weeks end-to-end typical for this class of POC
[00:15:25] Mark Holloway: that timeline works, we need internal stakeholder review at end of week 3 (security + infra)

[00:17:40] (discussion: success criteria recap)
[00:17:40] Alex Chen: recap suggested success criteria we will validate: 
- p95 latency < 450ms for responses < 100 tokens on 90% of requests
- p99 tail latency documented and under review threshold (target < 900ms)
- cost per 1M tokens at least 20% improvement vs current vendor in sustained runs
- VPC/KMS integration validated in staging
- No functional regression on output quality sample evals (we'll run a small eval set)

[00:20:05] (questions and clarifications)
[00:20:05] Sara Gomez: for the evals how many examples do you need to check quality drift?
[00:20:12] Priya Patel: usually 200-500 annotated examples across critical prompt sets is enough to flag regressions, we can metricize via BLEU/ROUGE or domain-specific heuristics and human spot checks

[00:22:00] (technical deep dive: concurrency, batching)
[00:22:00] Liam O'Neill: because you have a long tail, batching can help cost but increases latency — we'll tune batching windows by token-size tier: small requests (<80 tokens) use small batch window 10-50ms, medium 80-300 tokens can have slightly higher batching, and large we avoid batching to maintain latency; continuous batching optimizations help keep throughput high without big tail penalties
[00:23:15] Mark Holloway: any recommendations on model choice for a balance of throughput and quality? we were considering 13B int8 for most paths and 70B for investigations only
[00:23:25] Alex Chen: that pattern is common — 13B quantized for day-to-day with fallback to 70B for higher-fidelity or multi-turn investigations. We'll include fallback policy tests and measure switching cost (warm start + KV cache fill)

[00:27:40] (operational notes)
[00:27:40] Priya Patel: instrumentation: we'll surface token-level cost breakdown, trace samples for tail hops, and per-route dashboards. We'll add alerting for p95/p99 regressions and cost runaways during the POC
[00:28:10] Mark Holloway: great, budget question: approximate cost for 2-week full-run tests?
[00:28:18] Alex Chen: rough estimate depends on model mix; we'll send ballpark ranges in the spreadsheet but expect ~X to Y GPU hours — we'll quantify after we pick model configs. I'll include a conservative estimate for A100 vs H100 runs in the doc we send

[00:33:00] (network/connectivity checklist)
[00:33:00] Sara Gomez: checklist items for us: provide CIDR and peering details, create service account for Redwood tests, provide SAML contact for SSO test, provide sanitized logs and token histograms
[00:33:18] Mark Holloway: noted. we'll aim to deliver logs and CIDR by 2026-04-16

[00:38:00] (risks and mitigations)
[00:38:00] Tara Singh: potential risk is data residency and audit concerns, if private deployment required what's the rough lead time?
[00:38:12] Liam O'Neill: private on-prem can take longer (6-12 weeks depending on environment), VPC/private control plane is faster (2-4 weeks) if you have network ready. We'll recommend starting with hosted + VPC peering for the POC to reduce time to data

[00:45:00] (sample benchmark config that was agreed)
[00:45:00] Priya Patel: we'll run these configs: 
- 13B int8 on A100, small batch sizes, 1 replica
- 13B int8 on H100, compare throughput/cost
- 70B 4-bit on H100 for investigative flows (low qps)
- baseline smaller 7B quantized for low-cost ephemeral tasks
Each will have microbench (latency), steady state at 25 QPS and spike simulation to 120 QPS for 15 minutes

[00:49:30] Mark Holloway: works for us, please also show per-1k request cost and per-1M token cost so we can compare apples to apples
[00:49:40] Alex Chen: will do. Also include estimates for autoscaling behavior and warmup costs so the spike numbers reflect real world

[00:54:00] (wrap up and recap)
[00:54:00] Alex Chen: recap, next steps: 1) Mark share sanitized logs and histograms by 2026-04-16; 2) Alex to send benchmark template and cost ballpark by 2026-04-17; 3) Priya to schedule and run initial microbench in staging the week of 2026-04-20; 4) follow-up sync after baseline runs (end of week 1)
[00:54:32] Mark Holloway: we'll aim for those dates; one final ask — include a short section in the report that shows quality vs model size tradeoffs for 5-10 sample prompts
[00:54:45] Priya Patel: yes we will add the eval section and a small human check set
[00:55:00] Tara Singh: thanks all, this looks good, excited to see numbers
[00:55:08] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and kick off once we get the logs

[00:56:00] (end)
